question: Should dashboard activity/status widgets wait for the Wave 1 dashboard substrate and canonical sessions.activity/attention contract, or should maintainers approve an interim widget using existing sessions.list, Tasks, and Activity signals?
rationale: Current main only has coarse live/idle flags and browser-local tool Activity, while the requested widgets depend on unlanded dashboard APIs and an unsettled public activity-state contract.

options.title: Wait for dashboard plus activity contract
options.body: Implement the widgets after the modular dashboard substrate lands and #39127 defines the canonical busy, awaiting, progress, and child-session semantics.

options.title: Approve a coarse interim widget
options.body: Allow a limited widget using existing hasActiveRun, tasks, and browser-local signals, with explicit wording that it does not cover awaiting_user or awaiting_subagent semantics.

options.title: Fold into broader observability work
options.body: Defer this dashboard slice and consolidate the status/progress UI under #52960, #54577, or the broader orchestration trackers.

recommendation.title: Wait for dashboard plus activity contract
recommendation.body: Implement the widgets after the modular dashboard substrate lands and #39127 defines the canonical busy, awaiting, progress, and child-session semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The key blocker is the canonical gateway activity/attention contract tracked by #39127, which is assigned to vincentkoc.
